title: Relieve a distress
hookLine: whoever relieves a believer's hardship, Allah relieves his, and Allah helps a servant while he helps his brother
tomorrow: you meant to do a good thing and never did. does it count at all?

lines: A KNOCK ON A DEBTOR'S DOOR.
cards: Rent is due Friday, and a text lands: can you spot me till next month? Yesterday's question was who helps you while you help. Start with a story the Prophet told, peace be upon him, recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari.
A merchant used to lend money to people. His young men go out to collect. They knock on a door, and the man inside can't pay.
They go back to the merchant to report, and wait to hear what he'll do. And he says something they don't expect.

teach.h: LET IT GO. MAYBE ALLAH WILL LET US GO.
teach.b: He says: let it go. Maybe Allah will let us go. And the Prophet ends the story: so Allah let him go.
Hadith thirty-six, from Sahih Muslim, is the rule under that story.
Whoever relieves a believer of a distress of this world, Allah will relieve him of a distress on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever eases someone in hardship, Allah eases for him.

Whoever covers a person, keeps their hard moment private, Allah covers him. Then the line that answers yesterday's question: Allah helps the servant as long as the servant helps his brother. Notice the word.
Not after. While. The help isn't a payment that arrives later; it runs alongside you, right now, as you carry someone else's box.
The word for distress here is kurbah, the weight that tightens the chest.
And the line worth telling a friend tonight is the covering.
Relief isn't only money or muscle. Sometimes it's keeping someone's worst week out of the group chat.

how: Muslims point to this hadith when forgiving or delaying a debt for someone in hardship, helping a neighbor, or keeping a person's private struggles private.

o: lift someone's weight, and yours is lifted
pray for people instead of helping in person
lend money only when it's paid back on time

p: Allah helps you while you do
let it go; maybe Allah will let us go

s: in the story, the merchant collected every debt he was owed
he told his men to let it go, hoping Allah would let him go, and Allah did.
the hadith says Allah helps the servant as long as the servant helps his brother
covering someone means hiding harm they're still doing to others
covering means keeping a person's private slip or struggle private, not shielding ongoing harm.

games.q: a coworker made an embarrassing mistake, and you quietly fixed it. your manager asks what happened. what fits hadith thirty-six?
o: tell the whole story, names and all, so it's on record.
say it was your own mistake, so nobody looks bad.
say it's handled, and keep his slip covered without lying.
games.why: whoever covers a person, Allah covers him. covering is relief too, and it never needs a lie.

practice: Bring to mind one person carrying something heavy this week. Write them a short text, not advice, just: thinking of you, anything I can take off your plate?
Hold the phone for the sit, and let the decision to send it come in its own time.

wordCard.voice: Relieve a distress: lift a kurbah off someone, a weight on the chest, and Allah lifts one off you. Ease, cover, help.

orig.note: Arabic: whoever relieves a believer of a distress. kurbah is distress, a weight on the chest.

carryVoice: For the road: help, and be helped, because the help runs alongside you while you carry. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 2699 (Abu Hurayrah: whoever relieves a believer of a distress; Allah helps the servant as long as he helps his brother)
Sahih al-Bukhari 2078; Sahih Muslim 1562 (the merchant who told his men to let the hard-pressed debtor go)
